rationale: 4 real code defects (clone in-flight state shared across rows, Escape bypassing a disabled Cancel button, a blank failure toast on message-less errors, and an unvalidated clone response) plus 1 blocking standards commit-format violation force request-changes; all 7 story acceptance criteria pass and the security/code-quality standards are clean. 3 edge-case candidates were dismissed as noise: a harmless unmount setState (no React 18 warning path), a cosmetic pre-load canClone flicker, and a two-sources-of-truth concern already covered by the shared-ref fix (CR-003).

business_review.item: Clone opens a confirmation popup naming the source config; Cancel/Clone Server shown; no API call until confirm
business_review.notes: ConfirmationModal header/confirmText wired in MCPServerActions; onClone only in confirmClone; test confirms no early call.

business_review.item: Cancel closes the popup with no API call, no record created, no list entry
business_review.notes: cancelClone only hides the popup, never calls onClone; test confirms no call fires.

business_review.item: Both Cancel and Clone Server are disabled while the clone request is in flight
business_review.notes: confirmDisabled/cancelDisabled={isCloning} wired to ConfirmationModal; test confirms both disabled. See CR-002 for an Escape-key gap in this same path.

business_review.item: On success: popup closes, no edit window opens, list shows backend's verbatim/auto-named clone
business_review.notes: handleCloneServer only calls cloneConfig; store unshifts the raw API response; test confirms modal state untouched.

business_review.item: On failure: popup closes, a toast shows the failure message, no entry appears in the list
business_review.notes: catch+toaster.error without rethrow; finally always closes popup; store only unshifts on success. See CR-004 for a blank-toast edge case.

business_review.item: A clone's values change only through the existing, unmodified Edit MCP Server flow
business_review.notes: Diff never touches MCPServerModal; handleCloneServer never sets editingServer/showModal.

business_review.item: Clone row action uses dedicated clone.svg, distinct from Copy ID's unchanged copy.svg
business_review.notes: MCPServerActions imports CloneSvg from clone.svg?react; Copy ID keeps CopySvg unchanged.

standards_review.notes: Commit 'clone-mcp-config-ui: add planning artifacts' lacks the EPMCDME ticket prefix required by git-workflow.md's regex; the other 14 subjects in range conform.
No code-quality guide exists in the repo and no code_quality ArtifactRef was passed for this round.
Checked HTML sinks, cross-window messages, redirects and secret logging across changed files; no new unsafe sink/log introduced; a pre-existing console.log predates this change.

findings.title: Commit subject missing ticket prefix
findings.problem: Commit "clone-mcp-config-ui: add planning artifacts" lacks the required EPMCDME-NNNN ticket prefix mandated by git-workflow.md's commit-format regex.
findings.impact: The documented regex is enforced by the CI pipeline, so this subject blocks the commit-format gate for the merged range.
findings.recommendation: Reword or squash the commit so its subject follows "EPMCDME-15538: Capital sentence", e.g. during an interactive rebase or at squash-merge time.

findings.title: Escape key bypasses cancelDisabled
findings.problem: ConfirmationModal always wires Popup's onHide to the raw onCancel callback regardless of cancelDisabled, and Popup's own Escape handler (Popup.tsx:96-99) calls onHide whenever hideClose/visible/isTopmost hold, with no cancelDisabled check.
findings.impact: Pressing Escape while the clone confirmation is in flight closes the popup even though Cancel is explicitly disabled, so the request keeps running invisibly and its eventual success silently adds a row the user believed they cancelled.
findings.recommendation: Guard the forwarded onHide so it no-ops when cancelDisabled is true, e.g. onHide={cancelDisabled ? () => {} : onCancel} in ConfirmationModal.tsx.

findings.title: Clone in-flight state shared across rows
findings.problem: cloningRef/cloningId are single shared values; handleCloneServer's finally block unconditionally resets both to null regardless of which server's request just settled.
findings.impact: When two different rows' clones overlap, the first one to finish clears the still-in-flight second row's loading/disabled UI and re-enables its double-click guard, desyncing the Clone button state for a request that has not completed.
findings.recommendation: Key the guard and the finally-block reset on the specific server id (e.g. only clear when cloningRef.current === server.id), or track cloning state per-id in a Set/Record instead of a single ref.

findings.title: Clone failure toast can render blank
findings.problem: toaster.error(error?.response?.data?.message ?? error?.message) has no fallback string, so a rejection with neither a response payload nor a message (e.g. a bare network failure) passes undefined to toaster.error.
findings.impact: The user sees an empty/blank error toast with no indication the clone failed or why, missing the story's requirement that a toast show the failure message.
findings.recommendation: Add a default fallback, e.g. error?.response?.data?.message ?? error?.message ?? 'Failed to clone MCP server'.

findings.title: Clone response not validated before use
findings.problem: cloneConfig parses the clone response and unshifts it straight into configs without checking that result carries an id.
findings.impact: An empty or malformed clone response (e.g. a 200 with no body) produces a configless entry in the list, breaking row rendering and the id-based cloningId/cloning matching used across MCPServerActions and the table.
findings.recommendation: Validate the response before using it, e.g. if (!result?.id) throw new Error('Clone response missing id'), before unshifting.
